title: SQL lab: jump from filters to joins

turns.message: Jump ahead to joins now; I’ll guess the customer order query.
Give me a challenge on this.
I'll guess: putting status = 'paid' in WHERE is always equivalent to putting it in ON.
I’m stuck; why does COUNT(o.order_id) give zero for a customer with no orders?
Give me another challenge on this.
Correct answer: a LEFT JOIN preserves the left row, and a right-table filter in ON preserves unmatched customers.
/verify A right-table predicate in WHERE can remove the NULL-extended rows that a LEFT JOIN preserves.

expectations.notes: Honor the learner’s later SQL joins jump while briefly naming prerequisite grain; use the zero-orders customer to explain LEFT JOIN and COUNT(column); repair the ON-versus-WHERE misconception with a paid-order example.
